finding.claim: dropTable ignores the error returned by Authorize, so the 'dba' role check is never enforced. Any caller that reaches the handler can run DROP TABLE.
finding.source: Any HTTP client calling /admin/drop with an arbitrary 't' form value, with or without the 'dba' role.

trace.note: /admin/drop is registered with no auth middleware
userFrom does an unchecked type assertion on the context value
Authorize returns an error for non-dba users, but the result is discarded
Execution continues and the unsanitized table name is concatenated into the DROP TABLE statement

finding.guards_checked: Authorize is called but its error is not checked, unlike in vacuum (api.go:33-36), which does enforce it. There is no middleware, no input validation and no table allowlist. The SQL is built by string concatenation, so injection is also possible. For example, t="x; DROP TABLE users" gives stacked statements, depending on the driver. runSQL is a stub here.

verdict.guard_found: Authorize's error is discarded at api.go:26, but nothing in the code sets the "user" context value, so the nil type assertion in userFrom (api.go:22) panics at api.go:25 before the ignored check or the sink.
verdict.reason: The ignored Authorize error at api.go:26 is a real bug, but in this code, api.go:22 asserts a "user" context value that nothing sets (the only match for "user" or WithValue is that line). The assertion on nil panics at api.go:25, so runSQL at api.go:27 is never reached. The panic is a 500/connection abort, not a DROP. This refutes the exploit as stated: it only becomes exploitable if some auth middleware outside this code populates the context, and that is not in the code available.

verdict_facts.guard_found: none effective: Authorize (api.go:13-20) returns an error for non-dba users, but dropTable calls it as a bare statement at api.go:26 and discards the result. The route at api.go:44 has no middleware, and there is no allowlist or parameterization on the table name.
verdict_facts.reason: api.go:26 discards Authorize's error, so any authenticated user lacking 'dba' reaches runSQL("DROP TABLE " + r.FormValue("t")) at api.go:27 with an unvalidated table name, unlike vacuum, which checks the error at api.go:33-36.

finding.claim: The table name from the request is concatenated directly into SQL (SQL injection). Combined with F1, no privilege is needed.

trace.note: r.FormValue("t") is concatenated into the SQL string with no validation or identifier quoting

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist or identifier validation. The only authorization check is the ineffective one at api.go:26. runSQL is a stub, so the actual driver behaviour on multiple statements is unverified.

verdict.guard_found: Authorize(u, "dba") at api.go:26 returns an error, but the result is discarded as a bare statement, so it never blocks. There is no allowlist, quoting or parameterization on the table name. The /admin/drop route (api.go:44) has no middleware. userFrom (api.go:22) only reads the user from the context and does no check.
verdict.reason: api.go:27 concatenates r.FormValue("t") into "DROP TABLE " and runs it, and the Authorize result at api.go:26 is ignored (unlike the checked call at api.go:33), so any caller who reaches the handler can inject; runSQL (api.go:41) is a stub, so multi-statement driver behaviour is unverified, but an arbitrary table drop is already possible.

verdict_facts.guard_found: Authorize(u, "dba") at api.go:26 returns an error that is discarded, so it is ineffective. There is no allowlist, quoting or parameterization of the table name.
verdict_facts.reason: api.go:27 concatenates r.FormValue("t") into "DROP TABLE " + ..., and the only guard at api.go:26 discards Authorize's error. Any authenticated user can therefore reach /admin/drop (api.go:44) and inject arbitrary table names or SQL; whether extra statements run depends on the driver, but the identifier injection itself is not blocked.

finding.claim: userFrom does an unchecked type assertion on the context value. If no upstream middleware sets "user", the assertion panics, so any unauthenticated request to the admin routes triggers a panic. net/http recovers from it per request, which makes it a minor DoS or error-noise issue. No authentication middleware is present in this codebase.

trace.note: Routes are registered without auth middleware
The type assertion panics when the value is nil

finding.guards_checked: No comma-ok check and no authentication layer in this code. The context key is a plain string, so it could collide with other packages. A middleware outside this codebase may set it.

verdict.reason: api.go:22 does an unchecked `.(*User)` assertion, and api.go:44-45 register the routes with no middleware that sets "user", so an anonymous request panics and net/http recovers per request, which matches the claim's "minor" severity. Separate, more serious bugs exist that the finding doesn't cover: api.go:26 discards Authorize's result, and api.go:27 concatenates r.FormValue("t") into SQL.

verdict_facts.guard_found: Trusted upstream middleware (outside this directory, per project facts) populates the "user" context value, so the assertion at api.go:22 does not see nil. net/http also recovers handler panics per request.
verdict_facts.reason: The lines match the trace (api.go:22 does the unchecked assertion and api.go:44-45 register the routes), but the finding depends on the upstream middleware not setting the user. The maintainer states that middleware does set it, so api.go:22 doesn't panic for requests that reach it, and even a panic would be recovered per request. Separately, api.go:26 discards Authorize's result and api.go:27 concatenates input into SQL. Those are different findings and don't change this verdict.
